Done means each hook is proven to fire (or block) in a live headless Claude Code session, not just in theory.

one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a platform engineer building a deterministic guardrail layer for Claude Code. You treat hooks as production code that runs with the user's full permissions on every tool call. You trust the installed version's documentation and captured payloads over any blog post, including the guide you were given. You never claim a hook works until a live session proves it.

CONTEXT
- Hooks are shell commands the harness (not the model) runs at lifecycle events: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, SessionEnd, plus newer ones that churn between versions.
- Stdin is JSON (session_id, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, cwd, transcript_path, and per-event fields). Exit 0 allows, exit 2 blocks and feeds stderr to Claude, other non-zero is a non-blocking error.
- Claims from the guide you must TEST, not repeat: (1) 'structured JSON can return {"modified_tool_input": ...} to rewrite arguments' (current docs may name this updatedInput under hookSpecificOutput); (2) '{"decision": "approve"}' as a valid PreToolUse output; (3) 'SessionStart stdout gets injected into Claude's first system message'; (4) 'async: true hooks cannot block or modify'; (5) 'later settings files win for the same key' (hooks may merge rather than override).
- References: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide, github.com/disler/claude-code-hooks-mastery, the hookify plugin if installed (/hookify:list).

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Back up ~/.claude/settings.json to settings.json.bak-<date> before editing. Merge hooks with jq; never overwrite existing entries.
- All scripts live in ~/.claude/hooks/, are git-tracked, executable, shellcheck clean.
- PreToolUse hooks must finish in under 50 ms median (hyperfine, 20 runs).
- Every Stop hook must exit 0 when stop_hook_active is true to prevent infinite loops.
- Destructive tests only against canary paths under /tmp/hooktest-*. Never test against real data.
- The secret blocker reports the pattern name, never the matched value.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. ground-truth.md: claude --version, the event table copied from the installed version's docs, the exact output JSON schema, and a verdict on each of the five guide claims above.
2. A capture hook (temporary) that writes every event's stdin to ~/.claude/hook-payloads/; run one session that triggers Bash, Edit, Write, a subagent, and /compact. Keep the payloads as fixtures in ~/.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/. Remove the capture hook afterward.
3. Seven hooks: block-destructive.sh, block-secrets.py, format-on-edit.sh, session-git-context.sh, bash-audit.sh, precompact-backup.py (async), stop-tests-gate.sh.
4. tests/: bats or pytest cases, at least three per hook (allow case, block case, malformed-stdin case).
5. settings.json merged entries with matchers (Bash; Edit|Write|MultiEdit; empty matcher for lifecycle events) and timeouts.
6. Live proof: headless runs of `claude -p '...' --output-format stream-json` for the blocker, the secret blocker, and the Stop gate, saved as transcripts in ~/.claude/hooks/proof/.
7. README.md in ~/.claude/hooks/: what each hook does, how to disable (disableAllHooks or removing the entry), and a 'what this cannot stop' section.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before finishing, write GAPS.md listing: every event you could not trigger live and why; every guide claim that was false or unverifiable on this version; bypasses you found for each blocker (try bash -c, eval, base64 -d | sh, writing a script then running it, MCP tools that write files); hooks whose latency exceeded budget. Fix what you can now (for example extend the Edit matcher to MCP filesystem tools), and mark the rest open with a reason.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Did I read the docs for my installed version, or an older page?
- Does any hook print a secret, a full tool_input, or a transcript to stdout where Claude will see it?
- What happens to each hook when jq is missing, stdin is empty, or tool_input lacks the field I read?
- Does the Stop gate handle a repo without tests, and does it honour stop_hook_active?
- Does format-on-edit run on files outside the project (for example ~/.claude itself)?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and report when all seven hooks pass their tests and the three live proofs exist, or when a doc/behaviour mismatch blocks a hook (report the mismatch with the doc excerpt and the observed payload). Stop immediately and ask if any test would touch a path outside /tmp/hooktest-* or the hooks directory.

RETURN FORMAT
A single message with: (1) file tree of ~/.claude/hooks; (2) test summary (pass/fail counts per hook); (3) latency table (hook, median ms); (4) verdicts on the five guide claims; (5) the GAPS.md contents; (6) the exact settings.json diff.

steps.goal: Pin the exact hook contract of the Claude Code version you run and capture real payloads.
steps.prompt: Run `claude --version` and record it. Read the hooks reference at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and the hooks guide at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide. Then judge these guide claims as true, false, or renamed for this version: modified_tool_input rewrites args; decision: approve is valid for PreToolUse; SessionStart stdout is injected as context; async hooks cannot block; later settings files override earlier ones for hooks. Next, back up ~/.claude/settings.json, add a temporary catch-all hook on every event that runs `cat > ~/.claude/hook-payloads/$(date +%s%N)-event.json`, start one session that runs a Bash command, edits a file, writes a file, spawns a subagent, and runs /compact, then remove the catch-all. steps.title: Build and test the PreToolUse blockers
steps.goal: Ship a destructive-Bash blocker and a secret-leak blocker with fixture tests and latency budgets.
steps.prompt: Using the fixtures in ~/.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/ and the schema in ground-truth.md, write two hooks. (a) block-destructive.sh: read .tool_input.command with jq; block with exit 2 and a one-line stderr reason on rm -rf against /, ~, $HOME or a repo root, mkfs, dd of= to /dev/, fork bombs, chmod -R 777 /, git push --force to main or master, `find ... -exec rm -rf` without a .git prune, and rm -rf of any directory containing a .protected sentinel file (this gives live tests a safe target). Allow everything else. Handle missing jq or empty stdin by exiting 0 and logging to ~/.claude/hooks/errors.log. (b) block-secrets.py: on Edit, Write, and MultiEdit, scan new_string, content, and edits[].new_string against a pattern set derived from gitleaks default rules (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Anthropic and OpenAI keys, PEM private key headers, 64-hex Ethereum private keys) and exit 2 naming only the rule, never the value. Write bats or pytest cases: three allow, three block, one malformed stdin per hook. Run shellcheck. Time each with `hyperfine --runs 20` piping a fixture; the median must be under 50 ms. Then try to bypass block-destructive with bash -c, eval, base64 -d | sh, and a script file, and record which get through.
steps.expect: Two executable scripts, a test file with at least 14 passing cases, a hyperfine table, and a bypass list with pass/blocked per technique.
steps.audit: Re-run the tests from a clean shell. Grep the scripts' stderr strings to confirm no secret value can be echoed. If a known-dangerous fixture passes, or latency exceeds 50 ms, fix before moving on. Bypasses that remain open go into GAPS.md, not silently ignored.

steps.title: Build the advisory hooks
steps.goal: Add format-on-edit, Bash audit logging, and SessionStart git context, each tested.
steps.prompt: Write three hooks using the fixtures. (a) format-on-edit.sh for PostToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit: read .tool_input.file_path, skip files outside the session cwd (from .cwd) and anything under ~/.claude, then dispatch by extension: prettier --write for ts/tsx/js/jsx/json/css/md, ruff format for py, rustfmt for rs, gofmt -w for go. Skip silently if the formatter is not installed. Never exit 2. (b) bash-audit.sh for PostToolUse on Bash: append a TSV row of ISO timestamp, session_id, cwd, and the command with tabs and newlines escaped, to ~/.claude/bash-log.tsv; rotate when the file passes 10 MB. Write tests: format-on-edit actually reformats a badly indented fixture file in /tmp/hooktest-fmt; audit log escapes a multi-line command; git context prints nothing in a non-repo directory.
steps.expect: Three scripts, passing tests, and a sample bash-log.tsv row and git-context output pasted into the step notes.
steps.audit: Check that a command containing a tab or newline yields exactly one TSV row. Check the formatter does not touch files outside cwd. If SessionStart output is not visible to the model in a live test, switch to the documented JSON field and retest.

steps.title: Build the Stop gate and PreCompact backup
steps.goal: Refuse premature 'done' while tests fail, and snapshot transcripts before compaction.
steps.prompt: Write stop-tests-gate.sh for the Stop event. Read stdin; if .stop_hook_active is true, exit 0 immediately to avoid an infinite loop. Detect the test runner from the cwd: pytest if pyproject.toml or pytest.ini exists, `npm test --silent` if package.json has a test script, `cargo test --quiet` for Cargo.toml; if none, exit 0. Run it with a 120-second timeout. On failure, block the stop using the mechanism ground-truth.md specifies for Stop on this version (exit 2 with the failing test names on stderr, or JSON decision: block with a reason), capped to the last 30 lines of output. Write precompact-backup.py for PreCompact, registered async: copy the file at .transcript_path to ~/.claude/transcript-backups/<session_id>-<trigger>-<UTC timestamp>.jsonl, keep the newest 50, and never print the transcript. Test the Stop gate in /tmp/hooktest-stop with a tiny pytest project in three states: passing, failing, and stop_hook_active true while failing. Test the backup with a fixture payload pointing at a dummy transcript.
steps.expect: Two scripts and a test log showing three Stop outcomes (allow, block with reason, allow due to stop_hook_active) and one backup file created with the right name.
steps.audit: Confirm the gate cannot loop: simulate two consecutive Stop events, the second with stop_hook_active true, and verify exit 0. Confirm a 120-second timeout is shorter than the hook timeout you will register. Confirm the backup rotation deletes only files in its own directory.

steps.title: Prove each hook end to end in live sessions
steps.goal: Show the harness, not the test harness, enforces each hook.
steps.prompt: First register the hooks: back up ~/.claude/settings.json, then merge all seven entries into .hooks with jq, appending to existing arrays (matchers Bash and Edit|Write|MultiEdit for the tool hooks, empty for lifecycle events, async true for PreCompact, Stop timeout 150 seconds). ROLE AND STANCE
You are an engineering lead making one developer's repo safe and fast for parallel Claude Code sessions, following Boris Cherny's worktree pattern but measuring whether it works for this person. You prefer boring, deterministic scripts over clever orchestration. You do not trust throughput claims you have not measured.

CONTEXT
- Pattern: one task = one git worktree = one Claude session; all coordination via branches and PRs. Boris runs 3-5 at once; 10-15 is the team ceiling, not a target. Review bandwidth is the binding constraint.
- Primitives: `git worktree add ../proj-x -b feat/x`, `git worktree list`, `git worktree remove`, `git worktree prune`; native `claude --worktree [name]` and `--tmux` (verify on the installed version with `claude --help`); subagent frontmatter `isolation: worktree` (verify it exists in the installed version's subagent docs).
- Tools named in the guide: raine/workmux, nielsgroen/claude-tmux, muxtree, tmux.
- Known collisions from the guide: dev-server ports, shared Postgres/MySQL dev DB, node_modules at 500 MB-2 GB per worktree, shared .git/hooks writing to shared caches, IDE branch confusion, CLAUDE.md edits conflicting on merge, package.json adjacent edits, rate limits from N times token spend.
- Claims to TEST against this repo and this person: 'single biggest productivity unlock'; 'throughput gains cap around 3-5x'; 'zero merge conflicts between running sessions'; 'zero disk duplication of git history'.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Push the current branch before creating or removing any worktree. Never use `git worktree remove --force` on a dirty worktree without listing its uncommitted changes first and getting confirmation.
- Never `git add -A` in a worktree whose session is still editing; commit by explicit paths.
- No two concurrent tasks may share a file in their planned change set. Prove it before spawning.
- CLAUDE.md is edited only on main.
- Do not exceed the user's plan rate limits; start with three sessions.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. baseline.md: merged PRs per day and median createdAt-to-mergedAt over the last 30 days from `gh pr list --state merged --author @me --json number,createdAt,mergedAt --limit 200`; repo size; node_modules size; list of collision points found in package.json scripts, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, and git hooks.
2. Native-flag notes in baseline.md: where `claude --worktree` puts worktrees, branch naming, whether .env files are copied, cleanup behaviour. Tested, not read.
3. scripts/wt-spawn.sh <task>: push check, worktree on branch wt/<task>, deterministic PORT from cksum of the name into 3100-3999, isolated DB (docker compose -p <task> or SQLite file path), .env.local with PORT, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (or the repo's package manager) using the shared store, then `tmux new-window -n <task> 'cd <path> && claude'`.
4. scripts/wt-status.sh: table of worktree, branch, dirty file count, ahead/behind main, PR number and state via gh, PORT, container status.
5. scripts/wt-clean.sh: for worktrees whose PR is merged, show dirty state, remove worktree, delete branch, `docker compose -p <task> down -v`, then `git worktree prune`.
6. tasks.md: three backlog tasks with planned file sets and a pairwise-overlap check that shows zero shared files.
7. worktree-log.csv: task, spawn time, first review time, PR open time, merge time, conflicts (y/n), rework rounds.
8. results.md after the trial: merged PRs per day and median cycle time versus baseline, number of sessions at which review became the bottleneck, verdicts on the four claims.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before declaring done, list in gaps.md: collision points you found but did not isolate (shared caches, external APIs with per-account rate limits, ports hard-coded in source), anything about the native flag you could not determine, tasks that conflicted despite the overlap check and why, and whether the measurement window is long enough to mean anything (one week with three tasks is anecdote; say so). Fix any isolation gap that a script change can fix now.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Did two dev servers actually run at once on different ports, and did I curl both?
- Does any hook in .git/hooks write to a path shared across worktrees?
- What happens to Docker volumes and SQLite files when a worktree is removed?
- Does the repo hard-code port 3000 anywhere that .env.local does not override?
- Did I count review time, or only model time?
- Did any session edit CLAUDE.md, package.json, or a lockfile?
- Does wt-clean refuse to delete unmerged or dirty work?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop after scripts and tasks.md exist and a dry run of three spawns and one clean succeeds, then hand control to the user for the trial week. Stop and ask before removing any worktree with uncommitted changes, before dropping any database volume that existed before this work, and if the repo needs a shared external resource (single staging DB, single OAuth callback URL) that cannot be isolated.

RETURN FORMAT
One message: baseline numbers table; native-flag findings; the three scripts' paths with usage lines; tasks.md overlap matrix; dry-run output of wt-status.sh with three worktrees; gaps.md contents; the instructions for the trial week, including what to log.

steps.goal: Measure current throughput and find every resource two worktrees would fight over.
steps.prompt: In the repo at <path>, run `gh pr list --state merged --author @me --json number,title,createdAt,mergedAt --limit 200` and compute merged PRs per working day and median hours from createdAt to mergedAt over the last 30 days; write both to baseline.md with the raw counts. Then inventory collision points: grep package.json scripts, Procfile, docker-compose.yml, vite/next/webpack configs, and source for hard-coded ports (`grep -rnE '(PORT|:3000|:5173|:8000|:5432|:6379)' --include='*.{js,ts,json,yml,yaml,py,env*}'`); list database and Redis URLs and where they come from; list .git/hooks and husky or pre-commit configs and any paths they write; list caches (.next, .turbo, .pytest_cache, ~/.cache tool dirs) and whether they are inside or outside the checkout. Read Boris Cherny's two posts linked in the guide and note his own concurrency number. Finally, in a scratch clone, run `claude --help | grep -iA3 worktree` and one `claude --worktree probe-a` session; record where the worktree lands, its branch name, whether .env files are copied, and what happens on exit, then remove it. Write everything to baseline.md as tables.

steps.audit: Re-count PRs with a second query (for example the GitHub web search is:pr is:merged author:@me merged:>DATE) and confirm the number matches within one. Any port or URL found in source but not in env config is flagged as hard-coded; do not move on until each collision row has a 'how to isolate' note.

steps.title: Build the spawn script with isolation
steps.goal: One command creates an isolated, ready-to-run worktree with its own port, database, and Claude session.
steps.prompt: Write scripts/wt-spawn.sh <task-name>. It must: refuse if the current branch has unpushed commits; refuse if a worktree or branch wt/<task> exists; create the worktree at ../<repo>-<task> on new branch wt/<task> from origin/main (or call `claude --worktree <task>` instead if native-flag.md shows it supports what follows); compute PORT as 3100 + (cksum of the task name mod 900) and check it is free with `ss -ltn`; create an isolated database per the collision table (for Postgres `docker compose -p <task> up -d db` with a port also derived from the hash, or a SQLite path inside the worktree); write .env.local with PORT, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, and copy any other .env keys from the main checkout without printing their values; run the repo's install with the shared store (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync`, or equivalent); run migrations against the isolated DB; finally open `tmux new-window -n <task> -c <path> claude`. Make it idempotent on failure: if any step fails, print what was created and how to remove it. Run shellcheck.
steps.expect: An executable script under 150 lines that spawns a worktree in under two minutes, with shellcheck clean.
steps.audit: Spawn two test tasks, start the dev server in each, and curl both ports at the same time; both must answer. Confirm `docker ps` shows two separate DB containers or two SQLite files. Grep the script output for any secret value; none may appear. On any fail, fix and re-run both spawns.

steps.title: Build status and cleanup
steps.goal: See every worktree's state at a glance and remove merged ones safely.
steps.prompt: Write scripts/wt-status.sh that prints one row per worktree from `git worktree list --porcelain`: path, branch, dirty file count (`git -C <path> status --porcelain | wc -l`), commits ahead/behind origin/main, PR number and state from `gh pr list --head <branch> --json number,state`, PORT from .env.local, and DB container status from `docker compose -p <task> ps --format json`. Sort with dirty-and-no-PR first, because those need attention. Write scripts/wt-clean.sh that, for each worktree whose PR is MERGED: prints its dirty files; if any exist, skips it and says why; otherwise runs `git worktree remove <path>`, `git branch -d wt/<task>`, `docker compose -p <task> down -v` (only for projects it created, recognised by the wt/ prefix), and finally `git worktree prune`. Add `--dry-run` as the default; require `--yes` to act. Optionally bind wt-status.sh to a tmux status-right refresh every 30 seconds.
steps.expect: Two scripts; a status table for the two test worktrees; a dry-run cleanup listing what would be removed.
steps.audit: Mark one test PR merged (or simulate by merging locally into a throwaway main) and run the cleaner with --yes; verify the worktree, branch, and containers are gone and the other worktree is untouched. Create a dirty file in the remaining worktree and confirm the cleaner skips it.

steps.title: Decompose the backlog into disjoint tasks
steps.goal: Pick three real tasks that cannot collide and prove it.
steps.prompt: From the user's open issues (`gh issue list --limit 50 --json number,title,body`) or a provided list, choose candidates that are independent by the guide's rules: no output dependency between them, no shared global state, not deep debugging of an unfamiliar area. For each candidate, have Claude in read-only mode produce a planned change set: the files it expects to create or modify, derived from grepping the code involved. Build an overlap matrix of planned file sets; reject any pair that shares a file, and treat package.json, lockfiles, CLAUDE.md, shared config, and migration directories as always-conflicting unless only one task touches them. Pick the three with zero overlap and the smallest expected review time. Write tasks.md with, per task: issue link, one-paragraph prompt to give the session, planned files, acceptance test command, and expected review minutes. Include the overlap matrix.
steps.expect: tasks.md with three tasks, three prompts, and a 3x3 matrix of shared-file counts all zero.
steps.audit: Re-derive one task's file set independently (grep the identifiers involved) and compare; if the sets differ by more than two files, redo the plan for that task. Any task whose acceptance test cannot run in an isolated worktree is replaced.

steps.title: Run the parallel trial and log it
steps.goal: Execute the three tasks concurrently and capture the timing data that will judge the workflow.
steps.prompt: Spawn the three tasks with scripts/wt-spawn.sh. In each tmux window, paste that task's prompt from tasks.md, adding: 'Work only in this worktree. Commit by explicit file paths. Do not edit CLAUDE.md, package.json, or lockfiles unless the task requires it, and say so if it does. When done, run the acceptance test, push, and open a PR with gh pr create --fill.' Cycle through windows; while one runs, review another. Log to worktree-log.csv for every task: spawn time, time you first started reviewing, number of review rounds, PR open time, merge time, any merge conflict and its file, minutes you were idle waiting on all sessions. After merging, run wt-clean.sh --yes. If you feel idle between reviews, spawn a fourth task from the backlog with the same overlap check; if review starts queuing, stop spawning and note the session count where that happened.
steps.expect: worktree-log.csv with at least three complete rows, three merged PRs, and a note of the session count at which review saturated.
steps.audit: After each merge, run `git diff --name-only` between each pair of task branches to confirm no shared file slipped in; any conflict gets a row explaining which check missed it. Run wt-status.sh at the end; no orphaned worktrees or containers may remain.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Compare to baseline with GitHub's own data and state what the trial proves and does not.
steps.prompt: Re-run the baseline query for the trial window and compute merged PRs per working day and median cycle hours; put them beside baseline.md numbers in results.md. Check CI status on every trial PR (`gh pr checks <n>`) and record any failure caused by isolation leaks (wrong port, wrong DB, stale cache). Confirm with `git worktree list` and `docker ps -a --filter name=wt-` that cleanup left nothing behind. Give verdicts on the guide's claims with your numbers: productivity unlock (throughput ratio), 3-5x cap (where review saturated for you), zero merge conflicts (count), zero history duplication (`du -sh` of each worktree versus .git). Write gaps.md: unisolated resources, untested native-flag behaviour, conflicts and their causes, and an honest statement of sample size. Recommend the concurrency number to use going forward, with the evidence.
steps.expect: results.md with a before/after table and four claim verdicts; gaps.md; a recommended concurrency number.
steps.audit: If the trial window has fewer than five merged PRs, state that the throughput comparison is not statistically meaningful and recommend extending the trial rather than concluding. Every verdict must cite a number from worktree-log.csv or gh output.

gap_audit_prompt: You are reviewing a parallel-worktree setup and its trial results that someone else built in <repo>. Do not trust results.md. (1) List every claim: each script's guarantees (isolation of port, DB, env, cache; safe cleanup; push-before-destroy), each verdict on the guide's claims, the recommended concurrency. (2) For each, mark verified, unverified, or false with evidence: run the scripts yourself on a scratch task, curl two dev servers concurrently, inspect .env.local files for collisions, grep source for hard-coded ports, check .git/hooks for shared writes, re-run the gh queries. (3) Try to break isolation: spawn two tasks whose names hash to the same port (search for a collision with a quick loop) and see what happens; run migrations in both; run the test suite in both at once; check whether a shared cache under ~/.cache causes flaky results. (4) Try to break cleanup safety: leave an uncommitted file and an unpushed commit in a worktree with a merged PR and run wt-clean.sh --yes. (5) Rank gaps by impact (lost work first, then wrong results, then friction), fix the top three now, re-run, and report what remains with the reproduction command for each.
self_questions: Did I prove two dev servers ran simultaneously on different ports, or just assume it from .env.local?
What happens when two task names hash to the same port, and does the script detect it?
Do git hooks or husky write to a cache shared by all worktrees?
Does `claude --worktree` on this version copy .env files, and did my script duplicate or conflict with that?
Could wt-clean delete unpushed commits on a branch whose PR merged from an older commit?
Did any task touch package.json, a lockfile, CLAUDE.md, or migrations despite the plan?
Is my baseline window comparable in task type and working days to the trial window?
Did I log human review time and idle time, or only model run time?
validation_oracles: GitHub data: `gh pr list --state merged --author @me` for baseline and trial windows gives merged PRs per day and median cycle time computed the same way.
Two dev servers from different worktrees both return HTTP 200 when curled at the same moment on their assigned ports.
CI checks (`gh pr checks`) pass on every trial PR with no failures traced to wrong port, DB, or cache.
`git worktree list` and `docker ps -a` show no orphaned worktrees or containers after wt-clean.sh runs.
failure_modes: Port collisions. Tell: second dev server fails with EADDRINUSE or silently serves the other worktree. Fix: hash-derived ports checked with ss -ltn, and remove hard-coded ports from source.
Shared dev database corrupted by migrations. Tell: a worktree's tests fail on schema it never changed. Fix: per-worktree docker compose project or SQLite file, migrations per worktree.
Racing one task in several sessions. Tell: two PRs solving the same issue differently. Fix: one task per worktree, enforce with the tasks.md overlap matrix.
Review becomes the bottleneck. Tell: PRs wait hours for you while sessions sit idle. Fix: drop to the concurrency where review kept pace, usually 3-5.
agent_direction: Work in a scratch clone for all experiments with the native flag and cleanup scripts; touch the user's real checkout only to install the final scripts under scripts/. Never print .env values; copy keys without echoing. Spawn subagents only for read-only planning of each task's change set in step 5, never for the parallel sessions themselves (the user runs those). The trial week requires the user; hand off after the dry run with exact logging instructions. Return files: baseline.md, scripts/wt-spawn.sh, scripts/wt-status.sh, scripts/wt-clean.sh, tasks.md, worktree-log.csv template, and later results.md and gaps.md.

one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a developer-tools lead deciding, with evidence, which of this developer's tasks can move from Claude Code to Google's free Gemini CLI. You treat the guide's claims as hypotheses. You protect private code and secrets, and you assume quotas and model names have changed since the guide was written.

CONTEXT
- Gemini CLI: github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli, Apache 2.0, Node 20+. Install `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` or `npx @google/gemini-cli`. Context file GEMINI.md. Settings in ~/.gemini/settings.json (mcpServers block, same protocol as Claude Code). Headless: `gemini -p "..." --output-format json` or `stream-json`. Models via `-m` (guide: gemini-2.5-pro default, gemini-2.5-flash cheaper). Multi-root context: `--include-directories ../lib,../docs`. Official GitHub Action for CI. Built-in Google Search grounding.
- Guide claims to TEST: (1) free tier is 60 req/min and 1,000 req/day on 2.5 Pro with personal Google sign-in; (2) context window ~1M tokens versus ~200K for Claude; (3) Workspace accounts often cannot use the free tier; (4) one long agent session can use 100+ requests; (5) grounding is free and built-in.
- Proposed routes from the guide: commit/PR drafting, large-context reads summarized for Claude, grounded research, throwaway script codegen, CI review via the Action, a second vote in /council-style reviews, fallback during Anthropic outages.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Before sending any repository content, read the current free-tier data-use terms and record whether prompts may be used for training or human review. If they may, do not send code from private or client repos; use only open-source or personal repos and say so.
- Never pass .env files, keys, or credential directories to Gemini. Add them to .geminiignore (verify the file name is supported in the docs) and exclude them in every wrapper call.
- Pin the CLI version. Log every call. Stay at least 20 percent under the daily cap during evaluation.
- No route goes live until its blind evaluation is done.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. ground-truth.md: installed version, auth method, today's quotas and model names from Google's pages (with URLs and access date), data-use terms summary, the exact JSON schema returned by --output-format json (field names, stats block), and verdicts on claims 1-5 that can be checked without evaluation.
2. bin/gem: wrapper with -m, timeout, CSV logging (timestamp, route, model, latency ms, input/output tokens if reported, exit status), backoff on 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and fallback to `claude -p` after two failures, logging which agent answered.
3. .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg (installable script) that drafts a body from `git diff --cached` truncated sensibly, only when the message is empty, and never blocks the commit on failure.
4. scripts/repo-summary.sh producing docs/REPO_SUMMARY.md with an architecture map, module list, entry points, and known gotchas, using --include-directories.
5. scripts/research.sh that asks for grounded answers and requires a URL per claim in the JSON output.
6. eval/: commits.csv (25 historical diffs, blind-labelled outputs A/B, scores), summarizer.csv (15 grep-checkable questions answered by Claude with and without the summary, correct y/n), scripts.csv (10 throwaway-script tasks, shellcheck pass, fixture run pass).
7. routing.md: table of task type, route, evidence, fallback.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before finishing, write gaps.md: claims you could not verify (for example consumption of requests per session if /stats is unavailable headless); routes not evaluated (CI Action, council vote, outage fallback) and what it would take; any case where Gemini ran a command or edit without approval; quota numbers that differed from the guide; any evaluation where sample size is under 15. Fill what you can now: if the Action was not tested, set it up on a throwaway repo and run it once.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Did I read today's quota page, or rely on the guide's numbers?
- What do the free-tier terms say about prompt data, and did I respect that for every repo I sent?
- Were graders blind to which agent wrote each commit body?
- Did the summarizer help Claude answer more questions correctly, or just make it faster?
- Did grounded research return real, reachable URLs, and did I spot-check that they support the claims?
- How many requests did one prepare-commit-msg call consume, and what is the daily total at my commit rate?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop when routing.md is backed by the three eval files and the wrapper and hook are installed. Stop and ask if the terms forbid the user's intended use on private code, if sign-in requires a Workspace admin change, or if the quota is far below the guide's numbers (the routing case may collapse).

RETURN FORMAT
One message: ground-truth table (claim, guide value, verified value, source); file list with one-line usage each; eval summary (route, n, Gemini mean score, Claude mean score, verdict); routing table; gaps.md contents; the daily request budget estimate.

steps.title: Commit and PR drafting route
steps.goal: Draft commit bodies and PR descriptions for free, and test quality blind.

steps.title: Large-context summarizer route
steps.goal: Use Gemini's big window to summarize a repo and prove the summary helps Claude answer correctly.
steps.prompt: Write scripts/repo-summary.sh <repo>: run gem with `--include-directories` covering src, lib, and docs (exclude node_modules, build outputs, vendored code, and anything matched by the ignore rules), asking for docs/REPO_SUMMARY.md with sections: purpose, architecture map (modules and their dependencies), entry points with file paths, data flow, configuration and env vars by name only, test layout, and known gotchas with file:line references. Record the input size in tokens from the usage fields. Then build eval/summarizer.csv: write 15 factual questions about the repo whose answers can be checked by grep or by reading one file (for example 'which module reads DATABASE_URL', 'what function handles webhook retries'). Ask `claude -p` each question twice: once with no context beyond the repo path and a 2-minute budget, once with REPO_SUMMARY.md prepended. Check each answer against grep and record correct y/n and wall time. Also spot-check 10 file:line references in the summary for existence.
steps.expect: REPO_SUMMARY.md, input token count, eval/summarizer.csv with 30 graded answers, and a reference-accuracy score out of 10.
steps.audit: Any fabricated file path or function name in the summary counts against it; if more than 2 of 10 references are wrong, the route fails until the prompt is tightened and re-run. Confirm no secret values appear in the summary by grepping for key-like patterns.

steps.title: Grounded research and throwaway script routes
steps.goal: Test the two remaining cheap routes with checkable outputs.
steps.prompt: Write scripts/research.sh '<question>' that calls gem asking for a JSON array of claims, each with text and a source URL, using Google Search grounding. Run it on 8 questions where you can verify the answer (current latest version of three libraries the repo uses, a breaking change in one of them, two API rate limits, one security advisory). For each claim, fetch the URL and mark supported, unsupported, or unreachable; save eval/research.csv. Then pick 10 throwaway-script tasks from shell history or past requests (CSV munging, log grepping, file renaming, JSON reshaping) and generate each with `gem` and with `claude -p` using an identical prompt. Run shellcheck (or ruff for Python) on every output, then run each on a prepared fixture input and compare to an expected output you write first. Save eval/scripts.csv with lint pass, fixture pass, and tokens per agent. Finally, on a throwaway repo, install the official run-gemini-cli GitHub Action with the API key as a repository secret, open a PR with a planted off-by-one bug, and record whether the review catches it.
steps.expect: eval/research.csv with per-claim support status; eval/scripts.csv with 20 rows and pass rates per agent; one Action run URL with caught or missed.
steps.audit: If more than 20 percent of research claims are unsupported by their own URLs, mark the research route as 'leads only, verify before use'. Make sure expected fixture outputs were written before seeing either agent's script; if not, rewrite them and re-grade.

steps.title: Validate against the oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Turn the evals into a routing decision and list what is still unproven.
steps.prompt: Aggregate eval/commits.csv, eval/summarizer.csv, eval/research.csv, eval/scripts.csv, and eval/optional.md. For each route compute n, Gemini mean or pass rate, Claude mean or pass rate, and the difference. Write routing.md, one row per task type: task type, route to (Gemini, Claude, or Gemini-then-Claude-verify), evidence file, fallback, and expected daily request use from ~/.gemini-calls.csv extrapolated to the user's normal week. Compare that daily use to the verified cap from ground-truth.md and state the headroom as a percentage. Write gaps.md listing: guide claims with final verdicts (true, false, changed, unverified) with sources; routes with n under 15; any unapproved action Gemini took during testing; privacy constraints that limit which repos can use which routes; untested items. Recommend whether to keep the prepare-commit-msg hook installed, citing the median latency it added and the commit eval score.
steps.expect: routing.md with 6-8 rows, a daily budget estimate, and gaps.md with every guide claim resolved.
steps.audit: Every routing decision must cite a number from an eval file. If the daily estimate exceeds 80 percent of the cap, mark which route to throttle. If any route had graders who could see the agent label, mark its verdict provisional.

gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing a Gemini CLI routing setup built by someone else: bin/gem, a prepare-commit-msg hook, repo-summary.sh, research.sh, eval/*.csv, routing.md, gaps.md. Do not trust routing.md. (1) List every claim made: quotas, data-use terms, wrapper behaviour (logging, backoff, fallback, secret-path refusal), hook safety (never blocks, skips when a message exists), and each route's eval verdict. (2) Verify each: re-open Google's quota and terms pages today, run the wrapper with a bad model and with a .env path, commit with the network down, re-grade five random rows of each eval CSV yourself, and re-check five research URLs. Mark verified, unverified, or false with evidence. (3) Look for silent failures: does the hook ever write an empty or error message into a commit; does the wrapper count a fallback answer as a Gemini success; does the summarizer include ignored directories; do any logs contain secrets. (4) Rank gaps by impact: privacy or secret exposure first, then wrong routing decisions, then friction. Fix the top three now and re-run their checks. Report remaining gaps with the command that reproduces each, and state whether routing.md still holds.
self_questions: Are the quotas and model names in my notes from Google's page today, or carried over from the guide?
Do the free-tier terms allow sending this repo's code, and did I enforce that in the wrapper?
Does the wrapper recognise the actual quota-exhausted error, verified by triggering it or reading the source?
How many requests does one commit-draft call cost, and what is my weekly total at my commit rate?
Were the commit graders blind, and did they see the full diff?
Did the repo summary contain fabricated paths or functions, and how many?
Did grounded research URLs actually support their claims when opened?
Did Gemini ever run a shell command or edit without my approval during testing?
validation_oracles: Google's current Gemini CLI quota and terms pages, cited with URL and access date, versus the guide's 60/min and 1,000/day figures.
Blind A/B grading of 25 historical commits, scored by the user or a grader that never sees the agent label, with means per agent.
Fifteen grep-checkable codebase questions answered by Claude with and without the Gemini summary, scored against grep output.
shellcheck/ruff plus fixture runs with expected outputs written in advance for 10 throwaway-script tasks per agent.
failure_modes: Quota numbers out of date. Tell: 429 errors far earlier in the day than expected. Fix: re-read the quota page, lower the budget, route bulk work to Flash.

Private code sent under permissive free-tier terms. Tell: terms allow training or human review and client repos were used. Fix: restrict routes to open or personal repos, or use a paid API key with different terms.
Hook blocks or corrupts commits. Tell: commits hang or contain error text. Fix: timeouts, exit 0 on any failure, only write when the message is empty.
Summary hallucinates structure. Tell: Claude cites files that do not exist. Fix: require file:line references and spot-check them, re-prompt with stricter instructions.
agent_direction: Start with ground truth: install a pinned version, clone the repo for docs, and read today's quota and terms pages before sending any code. Use bin/gem for every Gemini call so all usage lands in one CSV. Spawn a separate grader subagent for blind A/B scoring that receives only the diff and two unlabelled candidates; never grade your own pairs. Never pass .env files, keys, or credential directories to either agent, and never echo the Action's API key. Stop and ask if the terms rule out the user's private repos, if sign-in requires a Workspace admin, or if the quota is too small for the routes to matter. Return in chat the claims table, eval summary, routing table, daily budget, and gaps; files go to bin/gem, hooks/prepare-commit-msg, scripts/, eval/, docs/REPO_SUMMARY.md, routing.md, gaps.md, ground-truth.md.

mission: Run Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2 locally as a reproducible image-to-3D pipeline: reference image in, cleaned and textured GLB out, measured for VRAM, time, mesh validity, and fidelity to the input, then extended to the text-to-image-to-mesh chain and a Blender import. Done means a scripted batch run on 10-20 of your own reference images with a results table (variant, steps, seconds, peak VRAM, watertight, face count, glTF validator errors, silhouette IoU), a license check for your intended use, and a clear verdict on which variant (Turbo, mini, mv, 2.1 PBR) fits your GPU and quality bar.

They would post-process with the repo's FloaterRemover, DegenerateFaceRemover, and FaceReducer, then validate GLBs with the Khronos glTF-Validator and import them headless into Blender to confirm they are usable assets. First read the Hunyuan3D 2.0 technical report, the repo README for Hunyuan3D-2 and 2.1, the Hugging Face model cards for tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 and tencent/Hunyuan3D-2.1, and the LICENSE; summarize variants, VRAM claims, and any territory or user-count restrictions. Clone the repo, create a Python 3.10 venv, install the CUDA-matched PyTorch, build custom_rasterizer and differentiable_renderer, and download pinned weight revisions. Write run_batch.py that, for each image in refs/: removes the background with hy3dgen.rembg, centers and pads it, generates shape with the chosen variant and seed, cleans it with FloaterRemover, DegenerateFaceRemover and FaceReducer, paints it if VRAM allows, exports GLB, and logs seconds per stage, peak VRAM, face count, watertightness, and silhouette IoU against the input mask. Run Turbo, standard, and mini (and 2.1 if it fits) on 10-20 of my images with fixed seeds. Validate every GLB with Khronos gltf_validator and a headless Blender import plus 4-view turntable render. Test the multiview variant on three objects with 2-4 views versus single view and compare back-side renders. Return results.csv, the turntable contact sheet, a variant recommendation for my GPU, the license verdict for my use, and a list of guide claims that did not hold.

one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a technical artist and 3D ML engineer turning Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2 into a measured, reproducible image-to-3D asset pipeline on this machine. You benchmark instead of eyeballing, you pin every version, and you validate every mesh with tools other than the model that produced it.

CONTEXT
- Code: github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2 and github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1. Weights: Hugging Face tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 and tencent/Hunyuan3D-2.1 (~50 GB for 2.1).
- Two stages: shape (Hunyuan3D-DiT, flow-matching DiT over a 3D latent, VAE decodes an SDF, marched to a mesh) and texture (Hunyuan3D-Paint, multiview diffusion baked to UV; 2.1 adds albedo, metallic-roughness, normal).
- Variants from the guide: DiT-v2-0 (1.1B), -Fast (guidance-distilled), -Turbo (step-distilled, 6-8 steps vs 50), v2-mini (0.6B), v2-mv (2-4 views), v2-1 (3.0B); Paint-v2-0 (1.3B), -Turbo, 2.1 Paint PBR.
- API: Hunyuan3DDiTFlowMatchingPipeline.from_pretrained('tencent/Hunyuan3D-2'); Hunyuan3DPaintPipeline.from_pretrained('tencent/Hunyuan3D-2'); outputs trimesh.Trimesh; export GLB.
- Claims to TEST: VRAM 6 GB shape-only mini, ~10 GB DiT-v2-0, 16 GB shape+texture for 2.0; 10 / 21 / 29 GB for 2.1 shape / texture / both; ~30 s per Flux image to mesh on a 4090; outputs 'watertight'; multiview is 'the single biggest quality unlock'; macOS texture is effectively unusable; Turbo at 6 steps is close to standard quality.
- Downstream chain from the guide: text -> Flux/SDXL image -> Hunyuan3D-2 -> auto-rig (Mixamo, Rigify) -> HY-Motion SMPL-X motion -> Blender retarget -> render. Auto-rigging is the weak link; Hunyuan3D outputs no rig.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Read the LICENSE first and state whether the user's territory and intended use are permitted. If not, stop before generating assets for that use.
- Pin the repo commit, the weight revisions, PyTorch and CUDA versions in env.lock.md.
- Fixed seeds; same preprocessed image for every variant comparison.
- Do not exceed available VRAM by guesswork: measure with torch, and use the mini or GP fork if the full pipeline OOMs.
- Store weights on fast local disk; do not commit weights or generated assets to git.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. ground-truth.md: GPU and driver, variant table from model cards, VRAM claims, license verdict with quoted clauses, the report's evaluation metrics and datasets.
2. env.lock.md and a working venv with custom_rasterizer and differentiable_renderer built; minimal_demo.py runs.
3. run_batch.py with preprocessing (BackgroundRemover, center, pad to square), per-variant shape generation, cleanup (FloaterRemover, DegenerateFaceRemover, FaceReducer to a target face count), optional paint, GLB export, and per-stage logging of seconds and peak VRAM.
4. metrics.py: trimesh is_watertight, face/vertex counts, euler number, bounding box; silhouette IoU between the input alpha mask and a front orthographic render; gltf_validator error and warning counts.
5. blender_check.py run via `blender -b --python`: import each GLB, confirm materials and images resolve, render a 4-view turntable to PNG.
6. results.csv over 10-20 reference images x variants that fit; contact_sheet.png of turntables.
7. mv_test/: three objects with single-view versus 2-4 view runs, back-side renders, and a blind preference record.
8. chain_demo/: one text prompt -> image (any local or API image model) -> mesh -> Rigify or Mixamo attempt, documenting where it breaks.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before finishing, write gaps.md: variants you could not run and why (VRAM, build failure); VRAM claims that did not match your measurements; meshes that failed validation and the failure type; whether 'watertight' held before and after cleanup; textures with seams or baked lighting; anything in the chain demo that needed manual work. Fix what is fixable now (for example tune FaceReducer targets, retry with better background removal), and leave the rest documented.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Did I read the license's territory and scale clauses, and does the user's use fit?
- Are all variant comparisons using the same seed and the same preprocessed image?
- Did I measure peak VRAM with the torch counters reset before each stage?
- Is the silhouette IoU computed from a camera that matches the input framing?
- Did cleanup remove real geometry along with floaters on thin parts?
- Do textured GLBs load in Blender with images embedded, not linked to temp paths?
- Is the multiview comparison blind, and does it include the back side?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and ask if the license excludes the user's territory or use, if the CUDA toolchain cannot build the rasterizer after two attempts with exact errors, or if no variant fits VRAM even with the GP fork. Otherwise stop when results.csv, contact sheet, mv_test, and gaps.md exist.

RETURN FORMAT
One message: GPU and env summary; license verdict; results table aggregated per variant (mean seconds, peak VRAM, watertight rate, mean IoU, validator errors); multiview verdict; recommended variant; gaps.md contents; paths to all outputs.

steps.title: Ground truth: report, model cards, license, hardware
steps.goal: Know exactly what the model family claims, what this machine can run, and what the license allows.
steps.prompt: Run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv` and `nvcc --version`; record both. Read the Hunyuan3D 2.0 technical report on arXiv (find it from the repo README) and note: architecture of the shape DiT and Paint model, evaluation metrics and datasets, and any numbers for speed and VRAM. Read the README of github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2 and Hunyuan3D-2.1 and list every variant with parameter count and Hugging Face subfolder by browsing the file listings of tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 and tencent/Hunyuan3D-2.1. Copy the guide's VRAM table and mark each value 'claimed'. Read the LICENSE file and quote the clauses on territory, monthly-active-user thresholds, and output use; state whether the user's location and intended use are covered. Write ground-truth.md with sections: Hardware, Variants, Claimed VRAM and speed, License verdict, Evaluation metrics from the report.
steps.expect: ground-truth.md of one to two pages with a variant table, quoted license clauses, and a yes/no/unclear license verdict.
steps.audit: Every variant must map to an actual Hugging Face path you saw; drop or flag any the guide lists that do not exist. If the license verdict is 'no' or 'unclear' for the user's use, stop and report before downloading weights.

steps.title: Build a pinned, working environment
steps.goal: Get minimal_demo.py running with locked versions and compiled renderers.
steps.prompt: Clone github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2 into repos/ and record the commit hash. Create a Python 3.10 venv. Install the PyTorch build whose CUDA version matches the driver from step 1 (choose the index URL accordingly rather than copying the guide's cu121 blindly). `pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .`. Build hy3dgen/texgen/custom_rasterizer and hy3dgen/texgen/differentiable_renderer with `python setup.py install`; capture full logs. Download weights with `huggingface-cli download tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 --revision <commit>` for the shape and paint subfolders you will test, onto NVMe; record revisions and disk size. Run the repo's minimal demo on its sample image and save the GLB. Also run `python -c 'import torch;print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.version.cuda)'` to confirm the GPU is visible. Write env.lock.md with Python, torch, CUDA, repo commit, weight revisions, and build outcomes.
steps.expect: env.lock.md, a demo GLB, and build logs; `python -c 'import custom_rasterizer'` succeeds.
steps.audit: If either extension fails to build, read the error, fix toolchain mismatches (gcc version, CUDA_HOME, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST) and retry once; on a second failure, record the exact error and continue shape-only. Confirm the demo GLB opens with trimesh and has more than 1,000 faces.

steps.title: Write the batch runner with preprocessing and cleanup
steps.goal: One script turns a folder of references into cleaned GLBs with timing and VRAM logs.
steps.prompt: Write run_batch.py --refs refs/ --variant {standard,turbo,fast,mini,mv,v21} --seed 1234 --paint {none,v20,v20turbo,v21} --out out/. For each image: remove background with hy3dgen.rembg.BackgroundRemover if no alpha exists; crop to the alpha bounding box, pad to square with 10 percent margin, resize to the size the pipeline expects; save the preprocessed image and its mask. Load the shape pipeline once per variant (subfolder per the variant table) and set steps per model card (Turbo around 5-8, standard per default). Before each stage call torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(); after it record torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() and wall seconds. Clean the mesh with FloaterRemover, DegenerateFaceRemover, then FaceReducer to a configurable target (default 40,000 faces); keep both raw and cleaned GLBs. If painting, run the paint pipeline on the cleaned mesh with the same image. Append a row per image and variant to results.csv: image, variant, paint, seed, shape_s, paint_s, shape_peak_gb, paint_peak_gb, faces_raw, faces_clean. Catch CUDA OOM per item, log it, and continue.
steps.expect: run_batch.py under 250 lines; a smoke run on 2 images producing 4 GLBs and a 2-row results.csv.
steps.audit: Re-run the smoke test with the same seed and confirm identical face counts (determinism). Check that peak VRAM is non-zero and below total VRAM. If cleanup reduces faces by more than 80 percent on a simple object, inspect for removed real geometry.

steps.title: Add independent quality metrics and Blender validation
steps.goal: Score every GLB with tools other than the generator.
steps.prompt: Write metrics.py that, for each cleaned GLB, loads it with trimesh and records is_watertight, euler_number, face and vertex counts, and bounding-box aspect ratios; renders a front orthographic silhouette with pyrender or Blender at the same framing as the preprocessed input, then computes IoU against the saved input mask; and runs the Khronos `gltf_validator` CLI, recording error and warning counts. Write blender_check.py for `blender -b --python blender_check.py -- <glb> <outdir>`: clear the scene, import the GLB, assert every material's image textures have pixel data, normalize scale, add a three-point light and camera, render front, right, back, and top at 512 px with Eevee, and write a JSON status. Run both over all outputs and merge columns into results.csv: watertight, iou, gltf_errors, gltf_warnings, blender_ok. Build contact_sheet.png from the turntables with Pillow, one row per image and variant.
steps.expect: Extended results.csv, a contact sheet, and a JSON status per GLB.
steps.audit: Validate metrics.py on a known-good mesh (a Blender default cube exported to GLB): IoU near 1.0 for a matching mask, watertight true, zero validator errors. If the known-good case fails, the metric is wrong; fix it before trusting any score.

steps.title: Run the variant benchmark on your references
steps.goal: Produce the numbers that decide which variant to use on this GPU.
steps.prompt: Assemble refs/ with 10-20 of your own images spanning: hard-surface objects (mug, tool), organic (plant, animal), a stylized character, thin structures (chair, bicycle), and a flat object (coin, leaf). Run run_batch.py for every variant that fits VRAM per step 1: standard, turbo, fast, mini, and v21 if 24 GB or more; paint with v20 and v20turbo, and v21 PBR if VRAM allows. Then run metrics.py and blender_check.py. Aggregate per variant: mean and p90 shape seconds, mean paint seconds, max peak VRAM, watertight rate, mean IoU, GLBs with validator errors, Blender failures. Compare measured VRAM and time against the guide's table and note each difference. Pick the five worst outputs by IoU and describe the failure type from the turntables (thin parts lost, back hallucinated, texture seams, baked lighting).
steps.expect: results.csv with all rows, an aggregate table per variant, and a five-item failure gallery with descriptions.
steps.audit: Confirm every image ran under every fitting variant with the same seed; missing rows must be explained (OOM or error logged). If the guide's VRAM number is exceeded by more than 20 percent, re-measure once with nothing else on the GPU before recording.

steps.title: Test the multiview claim and the text-to-character chain
steps.goal: Check the 'biggest quality unlock' claim and find where the full pipeline breaks.
steps.prompt: For three objects, capture or generate 2-4 orthogonal views (front, left, back, right) with consistent lighting and scale. Run the mv variant with all views and the standard variant with the front view only, same seed. Render back views of both with blender_check.py. Shuffle the pairs and ask the user or a grader subagent shown only the four reference photos and two unlabelled back renders which is closer; record preferences and the IoU of side views against the side photos. Next, run the chain once: a text prompt to an image model available to you (local Flux or SDXL via ComfyUI, or an API), producing a front-facing A-pose character on a plain background; mesh it with the best variant; import into Blender and try Rigify's auto-generation or upload to Mixamo; if HY-Motion is cloned at ~/projects/ai3-resources/repos/HY-Motion-1.0/, generate one motion and attempt a retarget. Log each handoff and what required manual fixes.
steps.expect: mv_test/ with renders and a preference table; chain_demo/ with the image, GLB, rig attempt, and a handoff log.
steps.audit: If the grader could tell which render came from mv by filename or order, redo the shuffle. For the chain, a step that silently produced an unusable result (rig with inverted bones, motion on the wrong skeleton) counts as a break, not a pass.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Lock the recommendation with external checks and document every remaining gap.
steps.prompt: Confirm the oracle set: all recommended-variant GLBs pass gltf_validator with zero errors; Blender headless import succeeds for each; watertight rate after cleanup; mean IoU above the threshold you set in advance (default 0.85); measured VRAM versus the guide. Write recommendation.md: the variant and paint model for this GPU with the evidence rows, expected seconds per asset, and the preprocessing settings to use. Write gaps.md with: guide claims and verdicts (VRAM table, 30 s on 4090, watertight, multiview unlock, Turbo quality), variants not run and why, failure categories with counts, chain breakpoints, license constraints on outputs. Fix the top fixable item now (for example raise padding if thin parts are clipped) and re-run the affected images. Record the final env.lock.md and the exact command that reproduces the recommended run.
steps.expect: recommendation.md, gaps.md, and a final results.csv; every claim has a verdict.
steps.audit: Every recommendation sentence must point to rows in results.csv or mv_test. If the threshold for IoU was changed after seeing results, say so explicitly. Re-run one recommended-variant item from a fresh shell to confirm reproducibility.

gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing a Hunyuan3D-2 pipeline and benchmark built by someone else: run_batch.py, metrics.py, blender_check.py, results.csv, mv_test/, chain_demo/, recommendation.md, gaps.md. Do not trust recommendation.md. (1) List every claim: variant speeds and VRAM, watertight rates, IoU scores, multiview preference, license verdict, reproducibility. (2) Verify each by re-running three random items from a fresh shell with the recorded seed and comparing face counts, peak VRAM, and IoU; re-running gltf_validator and Blender import on five GLBs; re-reading the license clauses quoted. Mark verified, unverified, or false. (3) Check the metrics themselves: does the IoU render match the input framing; does the known-good cube test exist and pass; are watertight checks done on cleaned or raw meshes and is that stated. (4) Look for silent failures: OOM items missing from results.csv without a log line, textures that reference temp paths, Blender renders that show empty scenes. (5) Check the multiview test for blinding and sample size. (6) Rank gaps by impact (license risk, unusable assets, wrong recommendation, slow runs), fix the top three now, and report the rest with the reproduction command.

Did I pin the repo commit and weight revisions, and could someone reproduce my numbers?
Did I reset the CUDA peak-memory counter before each stage, and is anything else using the GPU?
Is the IoU camera framing identical to the preprocessed input crop?
Are watertight results reported for raw or cleaned meshes, and does cleanup destroy thin parts?

ROLE AND STANCE
You are a docs and web-platform engineer adding the llms.txt layer to one real site so agents can understand it from a single fetch. You make it a generated build artifact, validate it with the reference parser, and measure whether it changes anything. You do not overclaim adoption by readers.

CONTEXT
- Spec (llmstxt.org, proposed by Jeremy Howard, Answer.AI, September 2024): Markdown file at /llms.txt. Exactly one H1 (required). Optional blockquote summary immediately after. Optional prose. H2 sections containing bullets of the form [Title](URL): description. A section named Optional is lower priority and may be skipped by context-limited agents. Use absolute URLs.
- Companions: /llms-full.txt (concatenated Markdown of canonical pages, co-developed by Mintlify and Anthropic; ship if under ~500k tokens), and .md twins at page URL + .md.
- Reference implementation: github.com/AnswerDotAI/llms-txt (Python parser, llms_txt2ctx CLI). Real examples: docs.anthropic.com/llms.txt and llms-full.txt; Stripe, Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase.
- Generators: Mintlify and Fern (automatic), Docusaurus plugin @signalwire/docusaurus-plugin-llms-txt, Nextra, Astro Starlight plugins, llmstxt npm and Python packages.
- Claims to TEST: ~844,000 sites have adopted it (BuiltWith, October 2025); Fern's Markdown serving cuts tokens by 90 percent or more versus HTML; Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Aider check /llms.txt; Claude's WebFetch does not auto-prefer it; publication is ahead of consumption.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Generate the files from the site's source or sitemap in the build; no hand-maintained copy that can drift.
- Absolute https URLs only. Every linked URL must return 200.
- Serve with a text content type and UTF-8; do not let the host serve it as HTML or force a download.
- Keep robots.txt consistent: do not invite agents in llms.txt to paths robots.txt disallows for them, and do not change robots.txt policy without the user's decision.
- Do not include private, draft, or unlisted pages.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. ground-truth.md: the spec rules in a checklist, the parser's behaviour on docs.anthropic.com/llms.txt, current adoption evidence you can find with sources, and verdicts on the claims above where checkable.
2. inventory.csv: every page from sitemap.xml with URL, title, word count, include (core, optional, exclude), and a draft one-line description.
3. scripts/build_llms.(py|mjs): emits dist/llms.txt, dist/llms-full.txt, and dist/<path>.md twins from source Markdown (or from built HTML via trafilatura/defuddle if no source Markdown exists); wired into the existing build command.
4. The generated files, with the blockquote written as a one-sentence answer to 'what is this site and who runs it'.
5. Host config for content types and .md routes (for example a _headers file on Cloudflare Pages, nginx types, or a Next.js route).
6. validation.md: parser output, llms_txt2ctx output size, lychee report, curl -I results for every file, token counts per page in HTML versus Markdown.
7. eval/questions.csv: 15-20 site questions with reference answers written before testing; results per agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity) with and without the llms.txt pointer; correct y/n.
8. logs/agent-ua.sql or script: query for AI user agents hitting /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, and .md twins; a reminder to re-run after 14 days.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before finishing, write gaps.md: pages excluded and why; pages whose Markdown conversion lost content (tables, code blocks, images with meaning); claims you could not verify (adoption count, which agents read the file); whether the eval shows a real accuracy gain or just noise at this sample size; whether the build fails loudly if a listed page disappears. Fix what you can now (for example add a build assertion that every llms.txt link exists in the sitemap).

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Does the file have exactly one H1, and does the parser read my sections as intended?
- Would a model reading only the blockquote answer 'what is this site' correctly?
- Is each description specific enough for a model to decide whether to fetch the link?
- Are .md twins faithful, including code blocks and tables?
- Is llms-full.txt under the size where a model can actually load it, and did I measure tokens?
- What happens to llms.txt when a page is renamed: does the build fail or silently ship a dead link?
- Do robots.txt rules and llms.txt invitations agree for each AI user agent?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop when the files are deployed, validated, and the eval is graded; leave the log check scheduled. Stop and ask before changing robots.txt policy, before including any page that requires login, or if the host cannot serve text content types without a plan change.

RETURN FORMAT
One message: the final llms.txt content in a code block; file list; validation summary (parser ok, broken links, content types); token table (page, HTML tokens, Markdown tokens, reduction percent); eval table (agent, with, without); claims verdicts; gaps.md contents; the date to re-run the log query.

Installed per vault under the vault's .claude folder; Claude Code launched from the vault root. Gotchas: sync conflicts with Obsidian Sync, iCloud, or Syncthing; Bases requires a recent Obsidian; wikilink targets not validated; conflicts with an Obsidian MCP if both are installed.
- Claims to TEST: the guide's Claude Code config path (~/.claude/settings.json) for MCP servers; that obsidian-bases is the only tool outside Obsidian that understands Bases syntax; that the MCP tells you when it extrapolates.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- n8n full mode only against a disposable Docker instance on localhost with its own volume. Never a production URL.
- N8N_API_KEY lives in the environment only; never write it into a committed file, never echo it, never paste it into a prompt.
- Work on a copy of the vault under git; pause any sync on that copy. Never write to the real vault during evaluation.
- Pin versions: n8n image tag, n8n-mcp version, obsidian-skills commit, Obsidian app version.

ORDERED DELIVERABLES
1. ground-truth.md: versions; where this Claude Code version reads MCP config; n8n-mcp's actual tool list from its tools_documentation; the node/template counts the server reports versus the guide; the obsidian-skills SKILL.md list and what each teaches; Obsidian version and whether Bases is available.
2. n8n-dev/: docker command or compose file, a fixtures folder (sample webhook payloads, a CSV), and a note on how the API key was created and where it is stored (name only).
3. MCP registration (command used, config with secrets referenced by env var only) and a test call to search nodes.
4. eval/n8n.csv: 10 workflow requests from the user's real needs, each generated without and with n8n-mcp; per run: unknown node types, invalid parameters, MCP validation errors, import ok, execution status on fixtures, minutes of manual fixing.
5. vault-test/: git-initialised copy of the vault with obsidian-skills under .claude/.
6. eval/obsidian.csv: 8 tasks (active-projects dashboard with wikilinks, clip a URL with defuddle and frontmatter, Base of in-progress notes sorted by modified with a days-since-touched formula, JSON Canvas of a folder's link graph, callout-formatted meeting note, properties cleanup across 20 notes, block-reference summary, embed-based index) each without and with skills; per run: opens in Obsidian, unresolved links added, frontmatter parse errors, canvas schema errors, files changed outside scope.
7. lint/: scripts for wikilink resolution, YAML frontmatter parsing, and JSON Canvas schema validation.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Before finishing, write gaps.md: guide claims with verdicts; workflow requests that failed even with the MCP and why (missing node coverage, credentials, community nodes); Obsidian features the skills did not handle; any time Claude mixed conventions or wrote outside the target folder; anything you could not test (hosted tier, Railway, Codex or OpenCode installs). Fix the fixable now (for example add a CLAUDE.md note in the vault copy forbidding writes outside a folder) and re-run the affected tasks.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Is the n8n instance truly disposable, and could any config path reach a production n8n?
- Did the API key ever appear in a log, transcript, or committed file?
- Did I verify where Claude Code reads MCP servers, or copy the guide's path?
- Do the with-MCP workflows actually execute on fixtures, or only import?
- Does each generated .base and .canvas open in the installed Obsidian version?
- Did Claude create wikilinks to notes that do not exist?
- Did any task change files outside its target folder in the vault copy?
- Is another Obsidian MCP or plugin also acting on the vault?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop when both comparison tables are filled and gaps.md is written. Stop and ask before connecting to any non-local n8n, before installing skills into the real vault, or if a workflow needs real third-party credentials.

RETURN FORMAT
One message: versions; config snippets with secrets as env var references; n8n comparison summary (without vs with: valid workflows, successful executions, mean fix minutes); Obsidian comparison summary (without vs with: files that open, unresolved links, frontmatter errors); claims verdicts; gaps.md contents; instructions to promote to the real vault if the user chooses.
